subproblems.title: Change of variables for an isometric embedding ℝ^P → ℝ^Q under μHE[d] (parent step 1)
subproblems.statement:
Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P, and Hᵈ = μHE[d] is Mathlib's normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and on ℝ^Q. Let P, Q, d ∈ ℕ and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be an isometry: |f(x) − f(x')| = |x − x'| for all x, x'. Linearity is not assumed. Then:
(i) f is a measurable embedding: injective, Borel measurable, and f(B) is Borel for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P.
(ii) For every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, with no measurability assumed, the push-forward under f of Hᵈ restricted to A is Hᵈ restricted to f(A): f_#(Hᵈ⌞A) = Hᵈ⌞f(A).
(iii) For every A ⊆ ℝ^P and every function g : ℝ^Q → ℝ, with no measurability or integrability assumed, ∫_{f(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫_A g∘f dHᵈ as Bochner integrals.
(iv) For every A ⊆ ℝ^P and every g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{f(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫⁻_A g∘f dHᵈ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q d : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → Euclid Q), Isometry f → MeasurableEmbedding f ∧ (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), Measure.map f ((μHE[d] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict A) = (μHE[d] : Measure (Euclid Q)).restrict (f '' A)) ∧ (∀ (A : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid Q → ℝ), ∫ y in f '' A, g y ∂μHE[d] = ∫ x in A, g (f x) ∂μHE[d]) ∧ ∀ (A : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid Q → ℝ≥0∞), ∫⁻ y in f '' A, g y ∂μHE[d] = ∫⁻ x in A, g (f x) ∂μHE[d]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (Hᵈ⌞L(A) = L_#(Hᵈ⌞A) and the resulting change of variables), i.e. the Jacobian-one case of the area formula behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(3) and 3.3–3.9 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 414–436 and 765–870). Here it is stated for an arbitrary isometry f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q; linearity is not used.
1. f is a measurable embedding. An isometry is injective and continuous. Since ℝ^P is complete, an isometry defined on it is a closed embedding: a homeomorphism onto its image, and the image is closed because it is complete (Mathlib Isometry.isClosedEmbedding). A closed embedding between Borel spaces is a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding): f is measurable, injective, and f(B) is Borel for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P. This is (i).
2. Push-forward of Hᵈ. For an isometry f, f_#Hᵈ = Hᵈ⌞range f (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). This holds because Hᵈ(f⁻¹(B)) = Hᵈ(f(f⁻¹(B))) = Hᵈ(B ∩ range f): isometries preserve Hᵈ of images (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
3. Restriction. For a measurable embedding f, every measure μ on ℝ^P and every set s ⊆ ℝ^Q, (f_#μ)⌞s = f_#(μ⌞f⁻¹(s)) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map; s need not be measurable). Take μ = Hᵈ and s = f(A). By injectivity f⁻¹(f(A)) = A (Function.Injective.preimage_image), so f_#(Hᵈ⌞A) = (f_#Hᵈ)⌞f(A) = (Hᵈ⌞range f)⌞f(A) by step 2. Since f(A) ⊆ range f (Set.image_subset_range), (Hᵈ⌞range f)⌞f(A) = Hᵈ⌞f(A) (Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset, valid for arbitrary sets). Hence f_#(Hᵈ⌞A) = Hᵈ⌞f(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P. This is (ii).
4. Bochner integrals. By definition ∫_{f(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫ g d(Hᵈ⌞f(A)), which equals ∫ g d(f_#(Hᵈ⌞A)) by (ii). For a measurable embedding f and any measure ν, ∫ g d(f_#ν) = ∫ g∘f dν for every function g (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). No measurability or integrability of g is needed: g is a.e.-strongly measurable and integrable for f_#ν exactly when g∘f is for ν, and otherwise both integrals are 0. With ν = Hᵈ⌞A this gives ∫_{f(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫_A g∘f dHᵈ. This is (iii).
5. Lower integrals. In the same way, ∫⁻_{f(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫⁻ g d(f_#(Hᵈ⌞A)) = ∫⁻ g∘f d(Hᵈ⌞A) = ∫⁻_A g∘f dHᵈ for every g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞] (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map, valid for every g). This is (iv). ∎
proof_key_steps: An isometry from the complete space ℝ^P is a closed embedding, hence a measurable embedding.
MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map with s = f(A), f⁻¹(f(A)) = A and Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset give f_#(Hᵈ⌞A) = Hᵈ⌞f(A).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and lintegral_map turn this measure identity into the integral identities for arbitrary g.

subproblems.title: Linear isometric embeddings transport approximate tangent spaces: T_{Lx}L(M) = L(T_xM) (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement:
Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ, blowUpMap x r (y) = r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT; Simon's η_{x,r}). A linear subspace S ⊆ ℝ^P is a d-dimensional approximate tangent space of M ⊆ ℝ^P at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d M x S, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) when dim S = d and, for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} f dHᵈ → ∫_S f dHᵈ as r → 0⁺.
Let P, Q, d ∈ ℕ and let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be a continuous linear map which is an isometry. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary, x ∈ ℝ^P, and S a linear subspace of ℝ^P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d M x S. Then the image subspace L(S) = S.map L is a d-dimensional approximate tangent space of L(M) at Lx: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d (L(M)) (Lx) (S.map L).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q d : ℕ) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid Q) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Isometry L → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d M x S → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d (L '' M) (L x) (Submodule.map (L : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid Q) S)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent-supplied proof (approximate tangent spaces are transported). It combines Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (the definition of the approximate tangent space, here SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt) with the Jacobian-one change of variables. Cf. T_y(f(M)) in Simon Ch. 6, 3.7 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 823–835).
1. Dimension. L is injective: Lw = Lw' gives |w − w'| = |Lw − Lw'| = 0. So L restricted to S is a linear isomorphism of S onto S.map L (Submodule.equivMapOfInjective). Hence dim(S.map L) = dim S (LinearEquiv.finrank_eq), and dim S = d by the first clause of the hypothesis.
2. Blow-ups commute with L. Let r ∈ ℝ and w ∈ ℝ^P. By linearity (map_sub, map_smul), blowUpMap (Lx) r (Lw) = r⁻¹ • (Lw − Lx) = L(r⁻¹ • (w − x)) = L(blowUpMap x r w). This holds for every real r, including r ≤ 0, because it is an identity between linear expressions. Taking images (Set.image_image), blowUpMap (Lx) r '' (L '' M) = L '' (blowUpMap x r '' M) for every r.
3. Pulling back the test function. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) and set g := f∘L. Then g is continuous. It also has compact support: L is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, ℝ^P complete), and a compactly supported function composed with a closed embedding is compactly supported (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding). Concretely, tsupport g ⊆ L⁻¹(tsupport f), and this set is compact because closed embeddings are proper. So g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
4. Change of variables. Apply part (iii) of the sibling change_of_variables (Submission.dor_lmb_fc_dtop_ip_isometry_change_of_variables) to the isometry ⇑L. For every A ⊆ ℝ^P it gives ∫_{L(A)} f dHᵈ = ∫_A f(Lw) dHᵈ(w) = ∫_A g dHᵈ.
 With A = blowUpMap x r '' M and step 2, for every r ∈ ℝ: ∫_{blowUpMap (Lx) r '' L(M)} f dHᵈ = ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} g dHᵈ.
 With A = S, using that the underlying set of S.map L is L(S) (Submodule.map_coe): ∫_{S.map L} f dHᵈ = ∫_S g dHᵈ.
5. Conclusion. The second clause of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d M x S, applied to g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), gives ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} g dHᵈ → ∫_S g dHᵈ as r → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0). By step 4 the function r ↦ ∫_{blowUpMap (Lx) r '' L(M)} f dHᵈ equals r ↦ ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} g dHᵈ for all r, and ∫_{S.map L} f dHᵈ = ∫_S g dHᵈ. Hence ∫_{blowUpMap (Lx) r '' L(M)} f dHᵈ → ∫_{S.map L} f dHᵈ as r → 0⁺. Since f ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) was arbitrary, this and step 1 prove HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d (L '' M) (Lx) (S.map L). ∎
proof_key_steps: dim L(S) = dim S = d because L is injective.
blowUpMap (Lx) r ∘ L = L ∘ blowUpMap x r for every r, so the blow-up of L(M) at Lx is L applied to the blow-up of M at x.
For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), f∘L ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) because L is a closed embedding.
The sibling change_of_variables turns the blow-up integrals and the limit ∫_{L(S)} f into the corresponding integrals of f∘L, so the hypothesis applied to f∘L gives the claim.

subproblems.title: Linear isometric embeddings transport unit orientations: ξ∘L^* orients L(S) (parent step 4)
subproblems.statement:
Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P. A d-covector of ℝ^P is a continuous alternating d-linear form on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) d). MultiVector P d is the space of continuous linear functionals on d-covectors of ℝ^P. For ξ ∈ MultiVector P d and a linear subspace S of ℝ^P, IsUnitOrientationOf ξ S means: there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ₀, …, τ_{d−1}) in ℝ^P with span(range τ) = S such that either ξ(α) = α(τ) for every d-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every d-covector α.
Let P, Q, d ∈ ℕ and let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be a continuous linear map which is an isometry. Let ξ ∈ MultiVector P d and let S be a linear subspace of ℝ^P with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ S. Let L^* = ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM L be the continuous linear map β ↦ β(L·, …, L·) from d-covectors of ℝ^Q to d-covectors of ℝ^P, and put (∧L)ξ := ξ ∘ L^* ∈ MultiVector Q d. Then IsUnitOrientationOf ((∧L)ξ) (S.map L).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q d : ℕ) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid Q) (ξ : MultiVector P d) (S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Isometry L → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ S → IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ.comp (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM L)) (Submodule.map (L : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid Q) S)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent-supplied proof (unit orientations are transported). This is the Jacobian-one case of Simon Ch. 6, 3.4–3.5 and 3.7 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 785–835): for an isometric L, L_#(τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_d) = Lτ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ Lτ_d is again a unit simple d-vector.
1. L preserves norms and inner products. L is linear, so L0 = 0, and the isometry property gives |Lx| = |x| for all x (Isometry.norm_map_of_map_zero). Therefore L is a linear isometry ℝ^P →ₗᵢ ℝ^Q, and ⟨Lx, Ly⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩ for all x, y by polarization (LinearIsometry.inner_map_map).
2. Unpack the hypothesis. IsUnitOrientationOf ξ S gives τ : Fin d → ℝ^P with τ orthonormal and span(range τ) = S. Moreover either (+) ξ(α) = α(τ) for every d-covector α of ℝ^P, or (−) ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every such α.
3. The new frame. Let τ' := L∘τ = (Lτ₀, …, Lτ_{d−1}). By step 1, ⟨Lτ_i, Lτ_j⟩ = ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = δ_ij, so τ' is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry).
4. The new span. range τ' = L(range τ) (Set.range_comp). The span of the image of a set under a linear map is the image of its span (Submodule.span_image). Hence span(range τ') = (span(range τ)).map L = S.map L.
5. The sign identity. Let β be a d-covector of ℝ^Q. By definition of composition of continuous linear maps (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply) and of L^* (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM_apply), ((∧L)ξ)(β) = ξ(L^*β) with L^*β = β.compContinuousLinearMap L. Also (L^*β)(v) = β(L∘v) for every v : Fin d → ℝ^P (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply), so (L^*β)(τ) = β(τ').
 In case (+), the hypothesis with α = L^*β gives ((∧L)ξ)(β) = (L^*β)(τ) = β(τ') for every β.
 In case (−) it gives ((∧L)ξ)(β) = −(L^*β)(τ) = −β(τ') for every β.
6. Conclusion. By steps 3–5, τ' is orthonormal, spans S.map L, and satisfies the same sign alternative for (∧L)ξ. This is IsUnitOrientationOf ((∧L)ξ) (S.map L). The argument is uniform in d; for d = 0, τ and τ' are empty and both spans are {0}. ∎
proof_key_steps: L preserves norms and hence inner products: it is a linear isometry.
τ' = L∘τ is orthonormal and span(range τ') = span(L(range τ)) = S.map L.
((∧L)ξ)(β) = ξ(β∘L) = ±(β∘L)(τ) = ±β(τ'), with the same sign as for ξ.

subproblems.title: Image IMRep of a linear isometric push-forward: (L(M), θ∘L*, (ξ∘L*)∘L^*) represents L#T and μ_{R'} = L_#μ_R (parent steps 2, 5, 6, 7)
subproblems.statement:
Conventions as in the parent: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]; 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d. An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d:
- a Borel, countably d-rectifiable carrier M ⊆ U;
- a measurable ℕ-valued multiplicity θ, positive on M and with finite lower integral over M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U;
- an orientation ξ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P d that is Hᵈ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, for Hᵈ⌞M-a.e. x, is a unit orientation of some approximate tangent space of M at x.
R represents X ∈ 𝒟_d(U) when X(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵈ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U). Its measure is μ_R = R.measure = (Hᵈ⌞M).withDensity θ.
Let P, Q, d ∈ ℕ and let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be a continuous linear map which is an isometry. Let hL be a proof that x ↦ 0 + Lx is proper. Let T ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (domain univ), and let R be an IMRep in ℝ^P (U = univ) representing T. Let L#T := GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward L 0 hL T ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^Q) (domain univ), i.e. L#T(ω) = T(L^#ω) with L^#ω(x) = ω(Lx)(L·, …, L·).
Then there is an IMRep R' in ℝ^Q (U = univ) that represents L#T and satisfies μ_{R'}(s) = μ_R(L⁻¹(s)) for every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q d : ℕ) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid Q) (hL : IsProperMap (fun x => (0 : Euclid Q) + L x)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d), Isometry L → R.Represents T → ∃ R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid Q)) d, R'.Represents (GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (V := (univ : Set (Euclid Q))) L 0 hL T) ∧ ∀ s : Set (Euclid Q), MeasurableSet s → R'.measure s = R.measure (L ⁻¹' s)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2, 5, 6 and the measure computation of step 7 of the parent-supplied proof. These are Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 and 3.3–3.9 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 403–436 and 765–870) for the injective map L with Jacobian J_L ≡ 1. In that case 3.8 reduces to the multiplicity θ(L⁻¹y) and the orientation L_#ξ(L⁻¹y). The accepted dtc_blowUp_imrep (for similarities of ℝ^P) has the same structure.
1. Facts about L.
(a) Apply the sibling change_of_variables (Submission.dor_lmb_fc_dtop_ip_isometry_change_of_variables) to the isometry f := ⇑L. It gives:
 - L is a measurable embedding;
 - (Hᵈ⌞A).map L = Hᵈ⌞L(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P;
 - ∫_{L(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫_A g∘L dHᵈ for every g : ℝ^Q → ℝ;
 - ∫⁻_{L(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫⁻_A g∘L dHᵈ for every g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞].
(b) L0 = 0, so |Lx| = |x| (Isometry.norm_map_of_map_zero). Thus L is a linear isometry and ⟨Lx, Ly⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩ for all x, y (LinearIsometry.inner_map_map).
(c) A continuous linear left inverse. Let L⁺ := L* : ℝ^Q → ℝ^P be the adjoint (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint; both spaces are complete). For x, y ∈ ℝ^P, ⟨L*(Lx), y⟩ = ⟨Lx, Ly⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left and (b)). Hence L⁺(Lx) = x (ext_inner_right).
(d) L is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), hence a proper map (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.isProperMap). So L⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^Q (IsProperMap.isCompact_preimage).
(e) Let C := L^* = ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM L. This is the continuous linear map β ↦ β(L·, …, L·) from d-covectors of ℝ^Q to d-covectors of ℝ^P. The map Φ : MultiVector P d → MultiVector Q d, ζ ↦ ζ∘C, is continuous (Continuous.clm_comp applied to continuous_id and the constant C).
2. Definition of R'. Write R = (M, θ, ξ). Let R' have carrier L(M), multiplicity θ'(y) := θ(L⁺y) and orientation ξ'(y) := ξ(L⁺y)∘C. By 1(c), for every x ∈ ℝ^P, θ'(Lx) = θ(x) and ξ'(Lx) = ξ(x)∘C = Φ(ξ(x)).
3. R' is an IMRep in univ ⊆ ℝ^Q. We check the fields of the contract structure IMRep univ d.
(a) measurableSet_carrier: M is Borel and L is a measurable embedding (1(a)), so L(M) is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image). carrier_subset: L(M) ⊆ univ.
(b) rectifiable: CountablyRectifiable d M gives M₀ with Hᵈ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^d → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j. Use L(M₀) and the maps L∘F_j. First, Hᵈ(L(M₀)) = Hᵈ(M₀) = 0 (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Second, each L∘F_j is Lipschitz, since L is 1-Lipschitz (Isometry.lipschitzWith). Third, L(M) ⊆ L(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j range(L∘F_j): if x ∈ M then x ∈ M₀ or x = F_j(v), so Lx ∈ L(M₀) or Lx = (L∘F_j)(v).
(c) measurable_mult: θ' = θ∘L⁺ is measurable, since θ is measurable and L⁺ is continuous.
(d) mult_pos: if y ∈ L(M), say y = Lx with x ∈ M, then θ'(y) = θ(L⁺(Lx)) = θ(x) > 0.
(e) locallyIntegrable_mult: let K ⊆ ℝ^Q be compact (K ⊆ univ). Since L(M) ∩ K = L(M ∩ L⁻¹(K)) (Set.image_inter_preimage), 1(a) gives ∫⁻_{L(M)∩K} θ' dHᵈ = ∫⁻_{M∩L⁻¹(K)} θ'(Lx) dHᵈ(x) = ∫⁻_{M∩L⁻¹(K)} θ dHᵈ. This is finite by locallyIntegrable_mult of R, because L⁻¹(K) is compact (1(d)) and contained in univ.
(f) aestronglyMeasurable_orient: by 1(a), Hᵈ⌞L(M) = (Hᵈ⌞M).map L. Since L is a measurable embedding, h is a.e.-strongly measurable for (Hᵈ⌞M).map L iff h∘L is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hᵈ⌞M (MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff). Here ξ'∘L = Φ∘ξ (step 2). This composes the continuous Φ (1(e)) with ξ, which is Hᵈ⌞M-a.e.-strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_orient of R). Hence it is a.e.-strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).
(g) orients: by orients of R, for Hᵈ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace S of ℝ^P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d M x S and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) S. For such x:
 - the sibling tangent_transport (Submission.dor_lmb_fc_dtop_ip_approxTangent_isometry) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d (L(M)) (Lx) (S.map L);
 - the sibling orientation_transport (Submission.dor_lmb_fc_dtop_ip_unitOrientation_isometry) gives IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)∘C) (S.map L), and ξ(x)∘C = ξ'(Lx) by step 2.
 Let p(y) be the property ∃ S', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d (L(M)) y S' ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(y)) S'. Then p(Lx) holds for Hᵈ⌞M-a.e. x. Since Hᵈ⌞L(M) = (Hᵈ⌞M).map L and L is a measurable embedding, MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff (no measurability of p required) gives p(y) for Hᵈ⌞L(M)-a.e. y.
4. R' represents L#T. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^Q) = TestFormOn univ d.
 By definition of the push-forward (GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply, which holds by rfl), L#T(ω) = T(L^#ω), where L^#ω = affinePullbackTestOn L 0 hL univ d ω. This is a test form on (x ↦ 0 + Lx)⁻¹(univ), which is definitionally univ. So L^#ω is an element of TestFormOn univ d, and the representation hypothesis of R applies to it: L#T(ω) = R.action(L^#ω).
 In Lean, state this identity as `have h1 : (GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (V := (univ : Set (Euclid Q))) L 0 hL T) ω = R.action (affinePullbackForm L 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid Q) d)) := hR (affinePullbackTestOn L 0 hL univ d ω)`, which typechecks by definitional unfolding. Do not use `rw [GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply]`: it fails because the domain change is only definitional.
 As a form, L^#ω(x) = affinePullbackForm L 0 ω x = (ω(0 + Lx)).compContinuousLinearMap L = C(ω(Lx)), using 0 + Lx = Lx. Define g(y) := θ'(y)·ξ'(y)(ω(y)). By step 2, for every x ∈ ℝ^P the integrand of R.action(L^#ω) is θ(x)·ξ(x)(C(ω(Lx))) = θ'(Lx)·ξ'(Lx)(ω(Lx)) = g(Lx).
 Hence R.action(L^#ω) = ∫_M g∘L dHᵈ = ∫_{L(M)} g dHᵈ by 1(a) with A = M, and the right side is R'.action(ω) by definition. So L#T(ω) = R'.action(ω) for every ω, i.e. R' represents L#T.
5. The measure. Let s ⊆ ℝ^Q be Borel. Then L⁻¹(s) is Borel because L is continuous. By definition μ_{R'} = (Hᵈ⌞L(M)).withDensity θ' and μ_R = (Hᵈ⌞M).withDensity θ. Then:
 μ_{R'}(s) = ∫⁻_s θ' d(Hᵈ⌞L(M)) (withDensity_apply)
 = ∫⁻_s θ' d((Hᵈ⌞M).map L) (1(a))
 = ∫⁻ θ' d(((Hᵈ⌞M)⌞L⁻¹(s)).map L) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map)
 = ∫⁻ θ'∘L d((Hᵈ⌞M)⌞L⁻¹(s)) (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map)
 = ∫⁻_{L⁻¹(s)} θ d(Hᵈ⌞M) (θ'∘L = θ by step 2)
 = μ_R(L⁻¹(s)) (withDensity_apply).
6. Steps 3–5 show that R' is an IMRep in univ ⊆ ℝ^Q that represents L#T and satisfies μ_{R'}(s) = μ_R(L⁻¹(s)) for every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Facts about L: change of variables (sibling change_of_variables), ⟨Lx, Ly⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩, the adjoint L* as a continuous linear left inverse, properness of L, and continuity of ζ ↦ ζ∘L^*.
R' := (L(M), θ∘L*, (ξ∘L*)∘L^*), so θ'(Lx) = θ(x) and ξ'(Lx) = ξ(x)∘L^*.

IMRep fields of R': Borel image; rectifiable cover by L(M₀) and L∘F_j; measurable, positive and locally integrable multiplicity via the change of variables and compact L⁻¹(K); a.e.-measurable orientation via aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff; a.e. orientation of L(S) via ae_map_iff with the siblings tangent_transport and orientation_transport.
Representation: L#T(ω) = R.action(L^#ω) by definitional unfolding; the integrand is g∘L with g = θ'·ξ'(ω), so the change of variables gives R'.action ω.
Measure: withDensity_apply, restrict_map and lintegral_map give μ_{R'}(s) = μ_R(L⁻¹(s)) for Borel s.
